questions.answer: Multiply each component by \(3\): \((6,-15)\).

questions.prompt: Compute \(-2(4\mathbf i-\mathbf j)\).
questions.answer: Distribute \(-2\): \(-8\mathbf i+2\mathbf j\).

questions.prompt: A vector \(\mathbf v=(3,4)\) is doubled. Find \(2\mathbf v\) and its magnitude.
questions.answer: \(2\mathbf v=(6,8)\). Its magnitude is \(\sqrt{36+64}=10\).
Multiply each component by \(1/2\): \((4,-3,5)\).

questions.prompt: A displacement \((5,0)\) m is multiplied by \(-1\). Interpret the result.
questions.answer: The result is \((-5,0)\) m, the same length in the opposite direction.
From \(2k=10\), \(k=5\). The second component gives \(3k=15\), confirming \(k=5\).

questions.prompt: A force \(\mathbf F=(4,-3)\) N is increased by a factor of \(2.5\). Find the new vector.
questions.answer: Multiply components: \(2.5\mathbf F=(10,-7.5)\) N.

questions.prompt: Find the unit vector in the direction of \(\mathbf a=(6,8)\).
questions.answer: Since \(|\mathbf a|=10\), the unit vector is \((6/10,8/10)=(3/5,4/5)\).

questions.prompt: Find a vector parallel to \((2,-1,2)\) with magnitude \(9\) and the same direction.
questions.answer: The original magnitude is \(3\), so scale by \(3\). The vector is \((6,-3,6)\).

questions.prompt: Determine whether \((12,-8)\) is a scalar multiple of \((-3,2)\).
questions.answer: The component ratios are \(12/(-3)=-4\) and \((-8)/2=-4\). Therefore \((12,-8)=-4(-3,2)\).
Equate components: \(4a=-12\) and \(4b=20\). Thus \(a=-3\), \(b=5\).

questions.prompt: For \(\mathbf u=(1,2)\) and \(\mathbf v=(-3,4)\), compute \(5\mathbf u-2\mathbf v\).
questions.answer: \(5\mathbf u=(5,10)\) and \(2\mathbf v=(-6,8)\). The difference is \((11,2)\).

questions.prompt: A velocity \((9,12)\) m s\(^{-1}\) is scaled to one third of its magnitude in the opposite direction. Find it.
Find \(t\) such that \(t(4,-2)\) has magnitude \(10\).
questions.answer: The base magnitude is \(\sqrt{20}=2\sqrt5\). Hence \(|t|2\sqrt5=10\), so \(t=\pm\sqrt5\).

questions.prompt: Verify \(2(\mathbf a+\mathbf b)=2\mathbf a+2\mathbf b\) for \(\mathbf a=(1,-3)\), \(\mathbf b=(4,5)\).
Find \(k\) so that \(k(3,4)\) has \(y\)-component \(-12\), then give the vector.
questions.answer: The equation is \(4k=-12\), so \(k=-3\). The vector is \((-9,-12)\).

questions.prompt: A line uses direction vector \(\mathbf b=(2,-1,3)\). Give two non-zero scalar multiples for the same line direction, then explain which one reverses the parameter direction.
questions.answer: Two examples are \(2\mathbf b=(4,-2,6)\) and \(-\mathbf b=(-2,1,-3)\). Both are parallel to \(\mathbf b\) and describe the same geometric line direction. The negative multiple \(-\mathbf b\) reverses the direction in which the parameter increases.

questions.prompt: Solve \(3(2x,1-x)=(12,-3)\), then decide whether \((2x,1-x)\) points in the same direction as \((12,-3)\).
questions.answer: The left side is \((6x,3-3x)\). From \(6x=12\), \(x=2\), and the second component gives \(3-3(2)=-3\), so the equation is consistent. Then \((2x,1-x)=(4,-1)\), and \((12,-3)=3(4,-1)\). The scalar is positive, so the vectors point in the same direction.

questions.prompt: A vector \(\mathbf a=(2,-2,1)\) is multiplied successively by \(k\) and \(m\), giving \((-18,18,-9)\). Find \(km\), and describe the effect on direction and length.
questions.answer: Successive scaling gives \(km\mathbf a\). Comparing first components, \(2km=-18\), so \(km=-9\); the other components agree because \(-2(-9)=18\) and \(1(-9)=-9\). The negative sign reverses the direction, and \(|km|=9\) makes the final vector \(9\) times as long as \(\mathbf a\).
